author: Computational Linguist
purpose: Shared ground-truth fixture for the stance-polarity-inversion bundle (epic t/2743). Consumed by the summary-pipeline gate (t/2739), the shared directional-agreement gate (t/2744), and the V-surface remediations (V1/V2 t/2745, V3/V4/V5 t/2746). Pins the observed origin inversion, the empirically-confirmed correct disposition (unmap + taxonomy gap), and the node_prop-richness requirement on the NLI gate (see nli_probe — the gate's recall depends on a contrastive label+Core node_prop, NOT on POV framing). Do NOT fork per-consumer copies — extend this file.
defect_class: A key point (or claim) that asserts the NEGATION of a taxonomy node's proposition embeds NEAR that node (cosine of a proposition and its negation is HIGH — shared content words), is selected by similarity, and is assigned/assumed 'aligned' with no direction (assert-P vs assert-not-P) check. All similarity-based gates false-green it.
contrast_with_saf_167_repro: saf-167-repro/case_1 was a LOW-retrieval-confidence miss: the wrong node was ABSENT from the key_point's bi-encoder top-80, so the t/2288 confidence gate FLAGS it. This case is the opposite and harder: the wrong node is the TOP topical match at HIGH confidence (0.7133 >> 0.45 gate) precisely BECAUSE it is the negation — topically near-identical. The confidence gate, the M5 top-3 pass, and the excludes-veto ALL pass it. Only a directional (NLI/entailment) signal catches it. That is why this bundle needs a new gate (t/2744), not a threshold tweak.

empirical_findings.observed_source: summaries/ai-doesnt-rewrite-privacy-law-it-changes-where-compliance-2026.json — pov_summaries.accelerationist.key_points[] entry with taxonomy_node_id 'acc-intentions-047'. Real pipeline assignment, human-inspectable.
empirical_findings.run_metadata: model_info: model=gemini-3.5-flash-lite, temperature=0.1, extraction_mode=fire (all_confident, 0 iterations), taxonomy_filter=rag, taxonomy_nodes=40 (doc-level RAG). acc-intentions-047 entered the 40-node candidate set on topic overlap (AI + privacy + law), then the LLM free-SELECTED it and assigned stance=aligned. This is an LLM-selection + stance-polarity error, and NOT a retrieval-confidence miss (confidence was high) nor an excludes-boundary case.
empirical_findings.taxonomy_gap_confirmed: Searched acc/saf/skp taxonomy for an anti-exceptionalism / 'adapt existing law to AI' counterpart node (terms: adapt+law, existing law, exceptionalism, ordinary+law). NONE exists — acc-intentions-047 (the 'new laws' pole) is the only near node. The correct positive home does not exist in the taxonomy; hence disposition = unmap + taxonomy gap (see t/2740).

nli_probe.finding: CORRECTED (t/2744#7, verified against the shipped scripts/nli_classify.py). The lever is node-proposition RICHNESS, NOT POV framing. A controlled 2x2 on the origin claim shows framing is INERT; the node's contrastive label+Core ('...Not Adapted Old Ones... rather than adapted existing laws') is what flips the verdict. The earlier 'framing-sensitivity' reading was CONFOUNDED — the two original probes differed in both framing AND node richness, so the flip was mis-attributed to framing.

controlled_2x2.claim_prop: Treating artificial intelligence as exempt from ordinary privacy law is fallacious because established data protection principles continue to govern responsible use.
controlled_2x2.rich_node_prop: Argue That AI Requires Entirely New Laws, Not Adapted Old Ones — asserts emerging technologies are so transformative they require entirely new legal frameworks rather than adapted existing laws.
controlled_2x2.bare_node_prop: AI requires entirely new legal frameworks rather than adapted existing laws.
controlled_2x2.conclusion: Framing had ZERO effect (rich->opposes both ways; bare->agrees both ways). node_prop richness fully determined the verdict.

label_only.note: MISSES the inversion — label alone is insufficient

label_plus_core.note: REQUIRED form: 'label — Core' (description with the Encompasses:/Excludes: tail stripped). Matches V1 calibration (PS smoke opposes@1.2746, tau_contra 1.0).

nli_probe.requirement: judgeDirection node_prop MUST be 'label — Core' (description with the Encompasses:/Excludes: tail stripped; label-only fallback), IDENTICAL across PS (V1/V2) and TS (V3/V4/V5) so every surface feeds the engine the same text (TL cross-surface ruling). The POV-framing wrapper is retained but is NOT the safeguard. Passing label-only or a terse/bare node_prop causes MISSED inversions.
nli_probe.recall_limitation: The gate under-catches when a node's description is terse/non-contrastive -> false 'agrees' -> the inversion keeps its edge. Accepted under the opposes-only fail-safe (the gate never falsely opposes; a missed inversion beats dropping every edge), but recall depends on node descriptions encoding the contrast. Enrich terse node descriptions to raise recall.

acc-intentions-047.label: Argue That AI Requires Entirely New Laws, Not Adapted Old Ones
acc-intentions-047.in_scope_core: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that asserts emerging technologies are so transformative they require entirely new legal frameworks rather than adapted existing laws. Proponents use this to justify sweeping regulatory changes tailored specifically for novel AI capabilities. Encompasses: bespoke AI legislation, regulatory sandboxes.
acc-intentions-047.excludes_clause: general arguments that caution hinders advancement or critiques of regulatory institutional inertia.
acc-intentions-047.note: The node asserts the 'new laws, NOT adapted old ones' pole. The observed source argues the exact opposite (no AI exceptionalism; existing law applies). The excludes_clause names sibling topics, NOT the negation — which is why the t/2286 excludes-veto (a sibling-topic test) cannot catch this inversion.

correct_counterpart_node.note: No positive 'adapt existing law to AI / anti-exceptionalism' accelerationist Intention node exists. Proposing one is t/2740. Until it lands, the correct disposition is unmap + unmapped_concept.

stored_key_point.verbatim: AI presents new privacy challenges, but treating AI as if it lives outside the parameters of ordinary privacy law is fallacious. The emerging lesson from privacy regulators and enforcers is increasingly clear: there is no AI exceptionalism. The same principles that have long governed responsible data use still apply. What changes is where those principles need to be built.
stored_key_point.canonical_proposition: Treating artificial intelligence as exempt from ordinary privacy law is fallacious because established data protection principles continue to govern responsible use.
stored_key_point.attribution_text: A Belief within accelerationist discourse that rejecting AI exceptionalism ensures existing privacy principles remain the baseline for technological deployment without requiring novel regulatory regimes. Encompasses: absence of AI exceptionalism, applicability of traditional privacy principles, operational translation over legal novelty.

wrong_output.category_mismatch: key_point.category='Beliefs' but acc-intentions-047.category='Intentions' — a corroborating symptom of a topical (not propositional) match.

unmapped_concept.concept: Anti-exceptionalism: AI is governed by ordinary privacy/data-protection law; existing principles continue to apply and should be operationalized in new places rather than replaced by novel AI-specific legal regimes.

fallback_if_counterpart_node_lands.note: If t/2740's anti-exceptionalism node lands first, map there with stance=aligned instead of unmapping.
fallback_if_counterpart_node_lands.alternative_on_acc_047: stance=strongly_opposed on acc-intentions-047 is also faithful (the source disputes that node's proposition), but is dispreferred due to the Belief-vs-Intentions category mismatch.

cases.NOT_a_repro_for: t/2288 retrieval-confidence gate (confidence was HIGH, 0.71) and t/2286 excludes-veto (excludes clause names sibling topics, not the negation). Neither can catch this — that is the point.

expectations.existing_gates: MUST all pass/false-green (documents the gap): retrieval_low_confidence=false @ 0.7133; M5 top-3 includes acc-intentions-047 (it IS the top topical match); excludes-veto MUST NOT fire.
expectations.judgeDirection_label_plus_core: MUST return direction='opposes' (NLI contradiction) when node_prop is the full 'label — Core' (conf ~1.42, above tau_contra 1.0).
expectations.judgeDirection_node_richness_guard: REQUIRED richness guard (replaces the retracted framing guard, t/2744#7): with a BARE node_prop the gate MISSES (returns 'agrees'); with the full 'label — Core' node_prop it CATCHES ('opposes'). See nli_probe.node_prop_construction. The V-surfaces MUST build node_prop as label+Core.
expectations.gate_action: On direction='opposes' where stance='aligned' was claimed: set stance_polarity_flag=true and either unmap (+unmapped_concept) or set opposed-family stance. Do NOT silently auto-flip without surfacing.

cases.notes: extraction_confidence 0.95 is the LLM's self-report — a different instrument from both retrieval_confidence and the directional gate. High self-report + high topical retrieval + WRONG direction is exactly the divergence judgeDirection exists to surface.

cases.provenance_evidence: Constructed negative control — a key point that genuinely ASSERTS acc-intentions-047's proposition. Exercises the gate's 'MUST NOT fire' arm (zero false-flag on true agreement).

query.canonical_proposition: AI is so transformative that it requires entirely new, bespoke legal frameworks rather than adapting existing laws.
query.attribution_text: An Intention within accelerationist discourse that novel AI capabilities demand purpose-built legislation and regulatory sandboxes rather than incremental adaptation of existing statutes. Encompasses: bespoke AI legislation, regulatory sandboxes, framework novelty.

expectations.judgeDirection: MUST NOT return 'opposes' (under POV framing a genuine agreement reads neutral -> direction='unrelated', per the t/2751#3 asymmetry ruling; the gate acts ONLY on 'opposes'). The correct assignment survives with zero false-flag.
expectations.gate_action: No flag; stance='aligned' stands (unrelated/agrees both mean 'no opposition detected' -> keep the edge).

cases.notes: Guards against an over-eager gate that flags genuine agreement. Required for the both-arms Gate Verification (t/2744).

cases.provenance_evidence: Constructed to exercise the fail-safe: when no directional signal is available (NLI engine unavailable AND node has no exclusion_vector), the gate MUST resolve 'unresolved', never 'agrees'.

expectations.gate_action: Caller MUST NOT assert agreement: downgrade to flag/neutral/unmap. Specifically closes the Find-SituationCandidates default-'entailment' fallback and the opt-in exclusion guard (t/2747).

cases.notes: Absence of a directional signal must never default to aligned — the load-bearing failure-semantics rule from t/2744#1.
